request.spec:
A button on each person's row downloads their statement as a CSV file: a header line
number,date,amount,figure,status then one line per claim of theirs bound by their last statement,
oldest first, with the bound figure as the claim shows it.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row now has an **Export statement (CSV)** button. Three of the four tests in `bin/e2e` pass, including the main "statement export" test. "Statement export scenario 3" fails on a rate check that this change doesn't touch. I didn't change the code behind that failure; you need to decide how it should behave.

**What I built** (all in `src/main/frontend/features/statements/statement.slot.tsx`, next to the Statement and Cancel statement buttons):
- The button (`person-export-statement`) re-reads the sheet from the store when pressed, like the existing people and claims exports.
- The file has the header `number,date,amount,figure,status`, then one line per claim of that person bound by their last statement, oldest first.
- The figure is worked out the same way as on the claim's row, so it shows the bound figure (or the settled due, once settled).
- No server or database change was needed: each claim already records whether it is bound and the figure it was bound at.

**Why scenario 3 fails** (`acceptance.spec.ts:1530`): with the screen viewed as of 2026-03-20, the test expects the rate calendar to show 12.50 for grade A in April 2026. It shows n/a.
- That 12.50 is a rate on the parent sheet. A new sheet starts its "today" on the real date, so the parent's today is 2026-10-25 and its rates count as set on that day.
- The as-of view only shows rates set on or before the as-of date (this rule is in `AsOf.rates`, `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/history/AsOf.java:190-201`). So the parent's rates are left out and the calendar shows n/a.
- The expected value would only come out if today's real date were on or before 2026-03-20. So the test seems to depend on when it is run.

I left that as-of rule alone because changing it changes how the as-of view works everywhere, not just in this feature. The fix would be to always include parent-sheet rates in the as-of view. That would make scenario 3 pass, but it goes against the rule as written. I can make that change if you want.
